3.text: If oxygen is not fully reduced (accepts one or two electrons), **reactive oxygen species** are formed: the superoxide anion radical O~2~^·−^, hydrogen peroxide H~2~O~2~ and the most dangerous — the hydroxyl radical ·OH. They cause lipid peroxidation and damage to proteins and DNA — **oxidative stress** takes part in atherosclerosis, complications of diabetes mellitus, aging and tumors.

6.text: The chemiosmotic theory. Inhibitors and uncouplers of the respiratory chain

According to **P. Mitchell’s chemiosmotic theory**, the energy released during electron transfer is used to pump protons across the inner mitochondrial membrane into the intermembrane space. As a result a **proton gradient** is formed — a pH difference (≈ 0.5–1) and a membrane potential (≈ 150–180 mV). When protons return through the channel of **ATP synthase**, ATP is synthesized from ADP and phosphate. Thus oxidation and phosphorylation are coupled through an electrochemical gradient.

parts.text: **2,4-Dinitrophenol** was once sold as a slimming drug and is still distributed illegally as a “fat burner”. It uncouples oxidation from phosphorylation and burns fat quickly, but causes uncontrolled **hyperthermia**; fatal poisonings have been reported.

blocks.text: At rest the membrane is permeable mainly to K^+^, so the resting potential is close to the potassium equilibrium potential. The contribution of several ions is taken into account by the **Goldman–Hodgkin–Katz equation**: the membrane potential is determined by the concentration ratio of each ion and by the membrane **permeability** (P) to that ion. The ion with the greatest permeability brings the potential closest to its own equilibrium potential.

blocks.text: The action potential obeys the **“all-or-none”** law: if the stimulus reaches threshold, a full response appears. Ion concentrations change only very slightly — the gradients are restored by Na^+^/K^+^-ATPase (one cycle: 3 Na^+^ out, 2 K^+^ in, 1 ATP used).

parts.text: **Local anesthetics** (lidocaine, procaine) block Na^+^ channels from the inside and stop the generation of action potentials and the conduction of pain impulses. They are weak bases: they cross the membrane in the **un-ionized** form but block the channel in the **ionized** form. That is why their effect weakens in acidic inflamed tissue (an abscess).
**Hypocalcemia** lowers the threshold for opening Na^+^ channels and increases excitability (tetany), while **hypercalcemia** does the opposite — it causes muscle weakness and constipation.

insert.title: 0. Electrolysis. Faraday’s laws. Corrosion of metals

blocks.text: **Electrolysis** is the redox process that occurs at the electrodes when direct current passes through an electrolyte solution or melt. Unlike in a galvanic cell, here electrical energy is converted into chemical energy: reduction occurs at the cathode (−) and oxidation at the anode (+). In the electrolysis of NaCl solution H~2~ and OH^−^ are formed at the cathode and Cl~2~ at the anode; Cl~2~ reacts with the alkali to give the disinfectant **sodium hypochlorite** NaOCl.

**Faraday’s laws:** the mass of substance liberated at an electrode is proportional to the quantity of electricity passed: m = M·I·t / (n·F), where I is the current (A), t the time (s), n the number of electrons per particle and F = 96 485 C/mol.

**Corrosion** is the destruction of a metal by electrochemical or chemical interaction with its environment. When different metals are connected through an electrolyte (saliva, tissue fluid), a **galvanic couple** is formed and the more active metal (the anode) dissolves.

parts.text: **Titanium** is the most widely used implant metal in medicine: the dense TiO~2~ film that forms spontaneously on its surface protects it from corrosion, and bone tissue bonds well to it (osseointegration).

cases.title: Problem 4
cases.text: In a neuron the Na^+^ concentration is 145 mmol/L outside and 12 mmol/L inside.
cases.ask: Calculate the sodium equilibrium potential at 37 °C. Why does the peak of the action potential not reach this value?
cases.answer: E~Na~ = 61·lg(145 / 12) = 61·lg12.1 ≈ 61 · 1.08 ≈ **+66 mV**. During depolarization Na^+^ channels open and the potential moves toward E~Na~, but the peak reaches only +30…+40 mV: Na^+^ channels inactivate quickly, and at the same time K^+^ channels open and the outflow of potassium pulls the potential back toward negative values.

cases.title: Problem 5
cases.text: In the Krebs cycle 2 electrons released from succinate pass to oxygen through FAD and ubiquinone. E°′(fumarate / succinate) = +0.03 V, E°′(½O~2~ / H~2~O) = +0.82 V.
cases.ask: Calculate the ΔG°′ of the process. Why does the oxidation of succinate yield less ATP than NADH?
cases.answer: ΔE°′ = 0.82 − 0.03 = 0.79 V; ΔG°′ = −2 · 96 485 · 0.79 ≈ −152 000 J/mol = **−152 kJ/mol**. For NADH ΔG°′ was ≈ −220 kJ/mol. Electrons from succinate bypass complex I and enter the chain at the level of ubiquinone — fewer protons are pumped and ≈ 1.5 ATP are formed (≈ 2.5 ATP from NADH).

cases.title: Problem 6
cases.text: To prepare an antiseptic in a ward, NaCl solution was electrolyzed with a current of 2 A for 30 minutes.
cases.ask: How much chlorine is liberated at the anode (M(Cl~2~) = 71 g/mol)? How does it turn into a disinfectant?
cases.answer: Q = I·t = 2 · 1800 = 3600 C; amount of electrons 3600 / 96 485 ≈ 0.0373 mol. At the anode 2Cl^−^ − 2e^−^ → Cl~2~, so n(Cl~2~) = 0.0373 / 2 ≈ 0.0187 mol, m = 0.0187 · 71 ≈ **1.3 g**. Chlorine reacts with the NaOH formed at the cathode: Cl~2~ + 2NaOH → NaOCl + NaCl + H~2~O — **sodium hypochlorite** is used to disinfect surfaces and instruments.

cases.title: Problem 7
cases.text: A young man who took “fat-burner” tablets at the gym was brought to hospital: temperature 41 °C, profuse sweating, tachycardia, rapid breathing. The tablets were found to contain 2,4-dinitrophenol.
cases.ask: Explain the mechanism of action of the substance from the point of view of the electrochemistry of the respiratory chain. Why did the temperature rise sharply?
cases.answer: 2,4-Dinitrophenol is a lipophilic weak acid; it picks up a proton in the intermembrane space, crosses the membrane and releases it in the matrix — it **dissipates the proton gradient**. Electrons continue to flow along the chain (O~2~ consumption even increases), but ATP synthase does not work: the energy of oxidation is converted not into ATP but into **heat**. To make up for the lack of ATP the body oxidizes more fat and glucose, producing even more heat — uncontrolled hyperthermia. There is no antidote; treatment is cooling and symptomatic.

cases.title: Problem 8
cases.text: A dentist tried to anesthetize the area of a purulent abscess with lidocaine, but the effect was insufficient. The pK~a~ of lidocaine is 7.9.
cases.ask: Calculate the fraction of the un-ionized form of lidocaine in normal tissue (pH 7.4) and in inflamed tissue (pH 6.9) and explain the result.
cases.answer: For a weak base lg([BH^+^] / [B]) = pK~a~ − pH. At pH 7.4: 7.9 − 7.4 = 0.5, ratio 10^0.5^ ≈ 3.2 : 1 — the un-ionized form ≈ 1 / 4.2 ≈ **24 %**. At pH 6.9: 7.9 − 6.9 = 1, ratio 10 : 1 — the un-ionized form ≈ 1 / 11 ≈ **9 %**. The anesthetic crosses the nerve membrane only in the un-ionized form, so in acidic inflamed tissue little of it enters the nerve and it cannot block the Na^+^ channels sufficiently. In such cases the anesthetic is injected farther from the focus of inflammation (conduction anesthesia).
